focus_area_title: Ensuring Follow-up to Employee Feedback on Patient Safety
content_text_body:
When employee feedback or suggestions are provided - on any topic - and there is no follow-up from leadership, the result is demoralization and disengagement.  Consistent follow-up to employee suggestions - **even if the suggestion can't be implemented** - will let employees know that their input regarding patient safety is valued.

[How to Solicit Feedback from the Team](video "LiL3_Solicit_Feedback")

**Watch**: *How to Solicit Feedback from the Team*

---

### Why is it important?

In their article in the Joint Commission Journal on Quality and Safety entitled, "Closing the Loopâ€ Gandi and co-authors found that while significant attention has been placed on reporting errors and "close calls,â€ more emphasis needed to be placed on what happens after a report is submitted.  When leaders "close the loopâ€ with employees regarding their patient safety input, that input is positively reinforced and the likelihood of reporting or "speaking upâ€ behaviors increases.  **A few tips for ensuring follow-up to employee feedback on safety are listed below:**

- **Make "Following-Upâ€ a Standing Agenda Item During Huddles/Meetings**

The Joint Commission Center for Transforming Healthcare's Safety Culture project found that two effective ways of reporting back to team members who raised safety issues were through 1) shift and unit huddles, and 2) visual management boards. They found that care team members stopped making suggestions when they received no feedback from team or hospital leaders.

- **Implement a "Good Catchâ€ or "Safety Heroesâ€ program within your team or organization and hard-wire "Following-Upâ€ in the program.  An example is below:**

Medical University of South Carolina Health (MUSC Health) issues a daily email highlighting a near-miss, error or unsafe condition and each month recognizes "safety starsâ€ - employees who have made these reports. **If care team members want closure in the reporting structure, they can ask to be personally notified with a result at the conclusion of the review.**

- **Respond as promptly as possible**

According to the article, "Leadership Role in Improving Safetyâ€ by the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, Issues raised by frontline staff during walkrounds must be promptly addressed, lest staff view the rounds as simply a visibility exercise for leadership. Similarly, voluntary error reporting systems often lack credibility among frontline staff due to insufficient follow up after an error is reported.

- **Have a unit leader or clinician follow-up with employees who report "close-callsâ€ or make safety suggestions**

"A unit director or clinician giving feedback to an employee who has reported a good catch makes it more impactful," according to Jacqueline Morgan, MSN, RN, CMSRN,

quality nurse coordinator II, patient safety, UPMC St. Margaret.  This type of follow-up to employee suggestions will increase the likelihood that they'll continue.

- **Make sure Patient Safety suggestions and Close-Call reports are tracked**

This will allow you and other leaders to review reports and suggestions to determine if policy/procedure changes should result from the feedback.  Furthermore, this practice will help ensure that you close the feedback "loopâ€ with employees and follow-up with them systematically, whether or not changes were made as a result of the feedback.

- **Create a process where you are regularly communicating with the hospital staff and clinicians about events and actions taken as a result of the feedback**

This will help employees understand the impact that their suggestions and increased reporting behavior has on the overall safety culture of the location.  Also, share not only the ideas/suggestions implemented but also share the total number of suggestions and reports and thank individuals for taking the time to share their feedback.

>Sources:

>"The essential role of leadership in developing a safety culture.â€ Joint Commission Sentinel Event Alert 57 (201
